headline: Recommended approval of a $2,082,498 bond for fire trucks and a $297,679 police mental health training grant, among other spending items.
summary: The committee recommended approval of every item on the agenda, each by a 5-0 roll call vote. Items covered legal bills, Community Preservation Act fund transfers, a zoning contract extension, school security equipment, fire trucks, and police grants.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the September 22, 2026 meeting, 5-0.
Recommended approval to pay $10,224.39 in prior year legal services invoices, 5-0.
Recommended approval of a $153,987 transfer from the CPA Community Housing Debt Service account to the CPA Community Housing Reserve, 5-0.
Recommended approval of a $22,596.24 transfer from the CPA Historic Preservation Debt Service account to the CPA Historic Preservation Reserve, 5-0.
Recommended approval of a time-only contract extension until 2/15/2027 for Utile Inc, 5-0.
Recommended acceptance and expenditure of a $169,000 grant for school security equipment, 5-0.
Recommended authorization to borrow $2,082,498 in a bond for an Aerial Ladder Truck and a Rescue Truck, 5-0.
Recommended acceptance and expenditure of a $297,679 grant for the Metro Boston Crisis Intervention Training and Technical Assistance Center, 5-0.
Recommended acceptance and expenditure of a $57,925 grant for the jail/arrest diversion program for Fiscal Year 2027, 5-0.

transcript:
## City of Somerville, Massachusetts City Council Finance Committee Meeting Minutes

Tuesday, October 6, 2026

6:00 PM

This meeting was held via Zoom and was called to order by Chair Wheeler at 6:00 pm and adjourned at 6:53 pm on a roll call vote of 5 in favor (Councilors Link, Strezo, Hardt, Scott, and Wheeler), 0 opposed, and 0 absent.

Councilor Link joined the meeting at 6:50 pm.

Others Present: Charles Breen – Fire Chief, Ed Bean – Director of Financ, Megan Huckenpahler – Director of Finance and Administration for Department of Public Works, Alan Inacio – Director of Finance and Community Development for Strategy and Development, Emily Wisdom – Director of Finance and Administration for Police, Madalyn Letellier – Assistant City Clerk, Legislative Services.

Roll Call

- Present: City Councilor At Large Kristen Strezo, Ward Seven City
- Councilor Emily Hardt, Ward Two City Councilor Jefferson
- Thomas (J.T.) Scott and City Councilor At Large Ben
- Wheeler

Absent:

City Councilor At Large Jon Link

1. Committee

Approval of the Minutes of the Finance Committee Meeting of September

Minutes

22, 2026.

(ID # 26-1450 )

- RESULT: ACCEPTED
- AYE:

- City Councilor At Large Link, City Councilor At Large
- Strezo, Ward Seven City Councilor Hardt, Ward Two City
- Councilor Scott and City Councilor At Large Wheeler

2. Office of Housing Stability

2.1. Mayor's Request Requesting approval to pay prior year invoices totaling $10,224.39 using

(ID # 26-1396 ) available funds in the Office of Housing Stability Ordinary Maintenance

Account for legal services.

Director Bean shared this was a billing at the end of the fiscal year that the original purchase order did not cover the full cost of the attorneys. In

response to Councilor Strezo, Director Inacio shared these payments are for legal services which are provided to residents with housing related

instability and there was a discrepancy in what was projected over what was billed.

RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE APPROVED AYE:

- City Councilor At Large Link, City Councilor At Large
- Strezo, Ward Seven City Councilor Hardt, Ward Two City
- Councilor Scott and City Councilor At Large Wheeler

3. Community Preservation Act

3.1. Mayor's Request Requesting the transfer of $153,987 from the Community Preservation Act

(ID # 26-1393 ) (CPA) Community Housing Debt Service account to the CPA Community

Housing Reserve.

Director Inacio stated the allocated amount for debt service was over and the funds can be transferred back to the Community Preservation Account to be

put towards projects. In response to Chair Wheeler, Director Inacio spoke to being conservative and over budgeted and now that there is a better idea of what the debt service will be the funds can be allocated back.

RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE APPROVED AYE:

- City Councilor At Large Link, City Councilor At Large
- Strezo, Ward Seven City Councilor Hardt, Ward Two City
- Councilor Scott and City Councilor At Large Wheeler

3.2. Mayor's Request Requesting the transfer of $22,596.24 from the Community Preservation Act

(ID # 26-1392 ) (CPA) Historic Preservation Debt Service account to the CPA Historic

Preservation Reserve.

Director Inacio stated the allocated amount for debt service was over and the funds can be transferred back to the Community Preservation Account to be

- put towards other projects.

RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE APPROVED AYE:

- City Councilor At Large Link, City Councilor At Large
- Strezo, Ward Seven City Councilor Hardt, Ward Two City
- Councilor Scott and City Councilor At Large Wheeler

4. Strategy and Planning

4.1. Mayor's Request Requesting approval of a time-only contract extension until 2/15/2027 for

(ID # 26-1391 ) Utile Inc to complete any outstanding task related to our up zoning and five

year zoning review efforts.

- Director Inacio stated this is related to a contract extension related to up
- zoning, five year review, and other ongoing zoning work.

RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE APPROVED AYE:

- City Councilor At Large Link, City Councilor At Large
- Strezo, Ward Seven City Councilor Hardt, Ward Two City
- Councilor Scott and City Councilor At Large Wheeler

5. DPW

5.1. Mayor's Request Requesting approval to accept and expend a $169,000 grant with no new

(ID # 26-1340 ) match required, from Urban Areas Security Initiative to the Department of Public Works for equipment to strengthen school security systems.

- Director Huckenpahler shared the funds will cover updating equipment

related to public address systems and made note in the body of the text it should read the Edgerly School not Winter Hill. Director Huckenpahler

confirmed there is no concern to completing the work before the grant times out in May.

RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE APPROVED AYE:

- City Councilor At Large Link, City Councilor At Large
- Strezo, Ward Seven City Councilor Hardt, Ward Two City
- Councilor Scott and City Councilor At Large Wheeler

6. Fire Department

6.1. Mayor's Request Requesting authorization to borrow $2,082,498 in a bond, and to appropriate

(ID # 26-1397 ) $2,082,498 for the purchases of an Aerial Ladder Truck and a Rescue Truck

for the Fire Department.

Director Bean stated progress payments have been made to the manufacturers, but the vehicle cannot be delivered before expiration of American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) funds, the plan is to borrow the money

- to complete the purchases. Remaining funds would be moved over to

Capital Projects so the funds would not be lost. Chief Breen highlighted the need for vehicles and the delay in service fulfillment due to the scarcity of vendors. In response to Councilor Scott this exchange will reduce the borrowing for the Poplar Street project but will still require an appropriation to complete the project.

RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE APPROVED AYE:

- City Councilor At Large Link, City Councilor At Large
- Strezo, Ward Seven City Councilor Hardt, Ward Two City
- Councilor Scott and City Councilor At Large Wheeler

- 7. Police Department
- 7.1. Mayor's Request Requesting approval to accept and expend a $297,679 grant with no new

(ID # 26-1413 ) match required, from the Mass Department of Mental Health to the Police

- Department for operational funding for the Metro Boston Crisis Intervention
- Training and Technical Assistance Center.

This item was discussed with item #26-1412.

- Director Wisdom stated the funds include salary, training, and operation

costs. Director Wisdom highlighted she came before the committee earlier in the year for request funds for a quarter of the year and these requests will

cover the costs of the entire year. Councilor Scott inquired about the allocated costs for salaries and Director Wisdom shared three roles as a part of Community Outreach, Help, and Recovery Unit (COHR) are fully funded

by the grant. These funds are in addition to what is covered in the budget, if the grants were not accepted the Police Department would have to come

- back in front of the Council after finding funds somewhere else.

RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE APPROVED AYE:

- City Councilor At Large Link, City Councilor At Large
- Strezo, Ward Seven City Councilor Hardt, Ward Two City
- Councilor Scott and City Councilor At Large Wheeler

7.2. Mayor's Request Requesting approval to accept and expend a $57,925 grant with no new

(ID # 26-1412 ) match required, from the Mass Department of Mental Health to the Police

- Department to fund the operation of the jail/arrest diversion program for
- Fiscal Year 2027.

This item was discussed with item #26-1413.

RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE APPROVED AYE:

- City Councilor At Large Link, City Councilor At Large
- Strezo, Ward Seven City Councilor Hardt, Ward Two City
- Councilor Scott and City Councilor At Large Wheeler
